reference.title: The use of quartz as an internal pressure standard in high-pressure crystallography

methods.source_location: Ross and Angel (1999), Experimental methods, journal page 278; pressures were obtained from measured quartz unit-cell volumes using Angel et al. (1997)
methods.notes: Angel et al.'s standard is a room-temperature BM3 with V0=112.981(2) A^3, K0=37.12(9) GPa, and K0_prime=5.99(4).

recalculation.notes: The exact quartz reference EOS is executable, but Ross and Angel Table 1 reports only reduced pressures and sample-cell measurements, not the row-wise quartz unit-cell volumes required to recalculate each pressure.

assessment.basis: Every compared free coefficient meets both the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison and parameter-specific numerical similarity screen. Error conventions and fit qualifications remain applicable.

scientific_validation.note: Validated directly against the final publisher article and its Table 1. The publisher page exposes no supplementary file. The article gives parameter errors but no confidence level or parameter covariance matrix, so the printed errors are preserved and covariance remains null.

primary_source_check.finding: The source defines an 11-observation, room-temperature, conventional-cell, three-free-parameter BM3 fit. Standard BM3 reproduces the source's 0.03 GPa maximum residual and weighted chi-square of 1.4.
primary_source_check.record_note: Coefficients from the abstract and Results (page 279), fitted to the 11 Table 1 observations with pressures from quartz volumes (Angel et al. (1997)). The standard Eulerian convention is confirmed by the source's 0.03 GPa maximum residual and weighted chi-square of 1.4.

primary_data_check.finding: All 11 printed CaTiO3 pressure, lattice-parameter, conventional-cell-volume, and estimated-standard-deviation values are transcribed. Row-wise quartz volumes are not published.

independent_refit.objective: effective-variance pressure residuals combining the reported pressure and volume estimated standard deviations; the ambient pressure has no printed error and is treated as fixed
independent_refit.conclusion: The independent refit recovers every published coefficient within its printed uncertainty and reproduces the source's rounded weighted chi-square.

parameter_provenance.determination_method: Measurements or their experimental reduction determine this EOS; source: Abstract; Experimental methods, journal page 278; Table 1, journal page 278; Results, journal page 279; Figure 1.
parameter_provenance.equation: Ross and Angel (1999), Experimental methods and Results, journal pages 278-279: pressure-dependent weighted least-squares fit of a Birch (1947) third-order Birch-Murnaghan EOS; reproduction of the reported residuals and weighted chi-square verifies the standard Eulerian finite-strain convention
parameter_provenance.V0: Ross and Angel (1999), abstract and Results, journal page 279: 223.764 +/- 0.017 A^3 conventional Pbnm cell; fitted
parameter_provenance.K0: Ross and Angel (1999), abstract and Results, journal page 279: 170.9 +/- 1.4 GPa; fitted
parameter_provenance.K0_prime: Ross and Angel (1999), abstract and Results, journal page 279: 6.6 +/- 0.3; fitted
parameter_provenance.temperature_ref: The article states room temperature without a numeric thermometer reading; 298 K is the operational room-temperature reference used by this record
parameter_provenance.fit_selection: All 11 CaTiO3 rows in Table 1, from 0.001 to 9.700 GPa

superseded_record_text.notes: Standard third-order Birch-Murnaghan pressure-volume EOS in the Eulerian finite-strain convention. V0, K0, and K0_prime were all fitted; none was fixed. V0 is one conventional orthorhombic Pbnm cell containing four CaTiO3 formula units. The paper reports no parameter covariance and does not state a confidence convention for the printed coefficient errors. The ambient pressure row has no printed pressure uncertainty; no zero uncertainty is invented in the dataset.
validity_notes: The numerical range is the exact Table 1 measurement envelope, not a phase-stability guarantee.
No phase transition or significant distortion change was detected through 9.700 GPa.
The 4:1 methanol-ethanol medium and single-crystal measurements define the experimental stress environment; extrapolation beyond the measured range is unvalidated.
